solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Display of gender inequality encapsulates current peeve (4)

indicatorNotes.encapsulates: to encapsulate is to enclose, so the display wraps round the current

blocks.note: one M (male) to two Fs (female): the sexes unequally shown
I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A campaigner is irritated by a chart showing the gender pay gap.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like social comment, but the "display" is literally letters: M beside FF shows the sexes out of balance. MIFF is informal for annoy.
annotation.definitionFit: To miff someone is to peeve them, to put them mildly out of sorts.

entries.clue: Bad behaviour of several types on Tube (10)

annotation.surface: Various kinds of rowdiness on the London Underground.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Tube look like the London Underground; here it is just a pipe.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: conduct is behaviour, and the mis- prefix makes it bad.

entries.clue: Attack in sports bar of criminal associate (5)

blocks.note: a barrier, such as a garden boundary, which bars the way

annotation.surface: A fight breaks out in a sports bar involving someone's crooked friend.
annotation.walkthrough: This is really three definitions strung together: fencing is a combat sport, a fence bars the way, and a fence handles a thief's stolen goods.
annotation.definitionFit: To fence is to attack with a sword in sport; a fence is also the dealer who buys stolen goods.

entries.clue: Suspect due bail holding everyone back is not to be praised (10)

indicatorNotes.Suspect: a suspect account is unreliable, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order
indicatorNotes.holding: one set of letters holds the other inside it
indicatorNotes.back: the word for everyone is read backwards

blocks.note: DUE BAIL rearranged; it splits after the I to hold the next piece

annotation.surface: A suspect whose bail is overdue is holding everybody up, and nobody is impressed.
annotation.walkthrough: ALL turned round sits after the I of the rearranged DUE BAIL.
annotation.definitionFit: Illaudable means unworthy of praise, from laudable with the negative prefix.

entries.clue: See female perhaps show liking for opera (9)

blocks.note: a hen is a female bird; 'perhaps' flags the example
to grin is to show you like something

annotation.surface: An invitation to watch a woman who may well take to opera.
annotation.walkthrough: LOHENGRIN is Wagner's opera about the swan knight.
annotation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is a romantic opera by Richard Wagner.

entries.clue: Passion visible in commercial broadcast (5)

indicatorNotes.visible in: the passion shows inside the advert, so it sits within it

blocks.note: a commercial is an advert, an AD

annotation.surface: An advert on television is full of raw emotion.
annotation.walkthrough: Commercial broadcast reads as one phrase, but broadcast is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a show put out on radio or television, past tense matching past tense.

entries.clue: Mocking of French cooking, but having no right (7)

indicatorNotes.having no right: the R (right) is taken out of the cooking word

annotation.surface: Someone sneers at French cuisine, but has no right to.
annotation.walkthrough: Mocking here means flouting, as in mocking the rules.
annotation.definitionFit: Defying authority is treating it with contempt, mocking it.

entries.clue: Helps nursing large sickly-looking bird (5,4)

indicatorNotes.nursing: to nurse is to hold close, so the helps word cradles the L

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

annotation.surface: Volunteers care for a big bird that looks unwell.
annotation.walkthrough: Nursing and sickly-looking make a hospital scene; the nursing only puts L inside BACKS.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this dark-plumaged Australian waterfowl is one kind of bird.

entries.clue: Like fish caught somewhere in East Anglia (4)

indicatorNotes.caught: to catch a remark is to hear it, so this is a sound

blocks.note: Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is said EE-lee

annotation.surface: A fish landed at some spot in the east of England.
annotation.walkthrough: Caught looks like the angler's word, but it means heard. Ely, in the East Anglian fens, took its name from the eels once caught there.
annotation.definitionFit: Eely means like an eel, slippery and fishlike.

entries.clue: Great sources for research into construction material (6)

indicatorNotes.sources for: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of research, into, construction

annotation.surface: Excellent references for studying building materials.
annotation.walkthrough: Construction material reads as one phrase, but construction supplies a first letter and material alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: material in the sense of cloth, the stuff garments are cut from.

entries.clue: Tanner starting run beats hides hard (9)

indicatorNotes.starting: to start is to jump, so the letters jump about
indicatorNotes.hides: the rearranged letters hide the H inside them

blocks.note: H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

annotation.surface: A leather tanner begins by running, then beats the hides hard.
annotation.walkthrough: Tanner and hides paint a leather workshop, but the tanner is someone getting a tan.
annotation.definitionFit: A sunbather lies in the sun to tan, so is a tanner.

entries.clue: Weak king charges let down (5)

indicatorNotes.charges: the king charges into the other word, landing inside it

blocks.note: to let someone down is to fail them

annotation.surface: A feeble monarch's accusations come to nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: Charges looks like a noun (accusations or fees); it is the verb, the king rushing into FAIL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone lacking strength, as an elderly invalid might.

entries.clue: Concerned about animal enclosure suffering infestation (7)

blocks.note: a run is a pen, such as a chicken run

annotation.surface: Worry about a livestock pen that has been invaded by pests.
annotation.walkthrough: OVER and RUN run together as one word.
annotation.definitionFit: A place overrun with rats is infested with them.

entries.clue: Fluid consumed in address regularly visited for bevvies (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly visited: only every other letter of address is visited

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of aDdReSs

annotation.surface: Liquid drunk at a house someone often goes to for a few drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: Bevvies is British slang for alcoholic drinks.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: bevvies is British slang, short for beverages, usually alcoholic ones.

entries.clue: Very large cat tucked into round lamprey, perhaps (10)

indicatorNotes.tucked into: the large cat is tucked inside the round word

blocks.note: a cycle is a round, a full circuit
a tom is a male cat

annotation.surface: A huge cat has got its teeth into a lamprey.
annotation.walkthrough: Very large cat reads as one big feline; very large is the outsize abbreviation, and the cat is a male one.
annotation.definitionFit: Cyclostomes are jawless fish with round sucking mouths, the lamprey being one.

entries.clue: Route some time entered by you and a learner bearing west (4,11)

indicatorNotes.entered by: the rest of the wordplay goes inside the time word

blocks.note: a day is a stretch of time
one's bearing is one's carriage, posture

annotation.surface: A road taken for a while by you and a learner driver heading west.
annotation.walkthrough: Bearing west looks like a compass heading; bearing is posture. DAY opens after its D to take the rest. A dual carriageway is a British divided highway.
annotation.definitionFit: A dual carriageway is a road with a central reservation, a route.

entries.clue: Case in Antrim settled, in which one is reprieved (9)

indicatorNotes.Case in: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.in which: the one sits in the settled word

annotation.surface: A court case in County Antrim is resolved and someone gets a reprieve.
annotation.walkthrough: Case looks like a legal matter; it means the outer shell of Antrim. Antrim is a county in Northern Ireland.
annotation.definitionFit: To be amnestied is to be granted an amnesty, officially reprieved.

entries.clue: Befuddled gent barred from drunken celebrating is crabby (9)

indicatorNotes.barred from: the gent's letters are shut out of the fodder
indicatorNotes.drunken: the remaining letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: as written, minus the letters of GENT
G, E, N, T removed in any order, hence befuddled

annotation.surface: A confused man is thrown out of a boozy party and is grumpy about it.
annotation.walkthrough: Befuddled says the letters of GENT come out of CELEBRATING wherever they fall, not as a run; IS joins the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Irascible means quick to anger, crabby.

entries.clue: Train old falcon not to turn aggressive (15)

indicatorNotes.to turn: the letters turn into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: Advice to a falconer: school the elderly bird so it does not turn nasty.
annotation.walkthrough: Old gives the O, a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Confrontational means inclined to face people down, aggressive.

entries.clue: Cylindrical package Vicky unwrapped is carpet (7)

indicatorNotes.unwrapped: the wrapping, Vicky's outer letters, comes off

blocks.note: a roll is a cylinder of something

annotation.surface: A rolled-up parcel that Vicky opens turns out to be a rug.
annotation.walkthrough: Carpet looks like the rug in the parcel, but it is the verb: to carpet someone is to give them a telling-off.
annotation.definitionFit: To rollick, like rollock, is to scold, which is what carpeting someone means.

entries.clue: Essentially flimsy ashen stick (6)

indicatorNotes.Essentially: the essence of a word is its heart, its middle

annotation.surface: A thin, grey-white stick.
annotation.walkthrough: Stick reads as a noun describing the stick; it is the verb, to pierce.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to pierce through with something sharp, as with a skewer or stake.

entries.clue: Inn employee initially ignored person shoving (6)

indicatorNotes.initially ignored: the first letter is left out

annotation.surface: A barman at first pays no attention to a pushy customer.
annotation.walkthrough: An ostler looked after guests' horses at an inn.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical job: the stableman who cared for travellers' horses at a coaching inn was on the inn's staff.

entries.clue: Go over river with mounting speed (5)

indicatorNotes.mounting: in a down clue, climbing means reading bottom to top

blocks.note: pace = speed, then written upward as ECAP

annotation.surface: Cross a river as the current gets faster.
annotation.walkthrough: Go over suggests crossing the river; it means summarise again.
annotation.definitionFit: To recap is to go over the main points again.

entries.clue: Domes, 13 shelters on high (7)

indicatorNotes.shelters: the drinks word shelters the other inside it

blocks.note: 13 across is DRINKS; colas are drinks

annotation.surface: Domes and roofs give cover up above.
annotation.walkthrough: 13 points to the answer at 13 across, DRINKS, which has to be turned into a kind of drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small dome on a roof.

entries.clue: Say romance is gripping subject (5)

indicatorNotes.is gripping: the romance word grips the other inside it

blocks.note: to romance is to tell tall tales, to lie

annotation.surface: A love story holds the reader's attention.
annotation.walkthrough: Romance is the verb, to embroider the truth. Liege works both ways: the lord, and the vassal bound to him.
annotation.definitionFit: A liege can be a vassal owing feudal service, a subject.

entries.clue: Tungsten half of striking tool forcibly hit (4)

indicatorNotes.half of: only the first half of the tool's name is used

blocks.note: W is the chemical symbol for tungsten

annotation.surface: Half a tungsten hammer makes a violent blow.
annotation.walkthrough: W comes from tungsten's old name, wolfram.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal verb: the comic-book sound of a heavy blow became a word for delivering one.

entries.clue: Rejecting outsiders, chap with his land (5)

indicatorNotes.Rejecting outsiders: each word loses its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A xenophobic man keeps his country to himself.
annotation.walkthrough: Rejecting outsiders reads as xenophobia; it strips the ends off the next three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Caribbean republic sharing Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic is a land, a country.

entries.clue: Horseman in a party I’m unsure should be in company (9)

indicatorNotes.should be in: everything before it goes inside the company word

blocks.note: a ball is a dance party

annotation.surface: A rider at a party is not sure he belongs in such company.
annotation.walkthrough: A party tempts CABAL, but that leaves LER to explain; the party is a BALL.
annotation.definitionFit: A caballero is a Spanish gentleman, originally a horseman or knight.

entries.clue: Semiaquatic creature spiked rump badly (10)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are put together badly, out of order

annotation.surface: An amphibious beast with a painfully spiny backside.
annotation.walkthrough: Spiked rump sounds like a description of the creature, but it is only the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The mudskipper is a fish that spends much of its time out of water on mudflats.

entries.clue: Shrub male insect snubbed (4)

indicatorNotes.snubbed: to snub is to cut short, so the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A bush where a male insect is given the cold shoulder.
annotation.walkthrough: Snubbed puns on snub, a short stubby nose: the insect loses its tail.
annotation.definitionFit: Hebe is a genus of evergreen shrubs from New Zealand.
